props.title: The People That Time Forgot
props.initialSlug: Sequel to Land That Time Forgot

sections.content: **The People That Time Forgot** (1977) represents a fascinating entry in Amicus Productions' Edgar Rice Burroughs adaptations, following **The Land That Time Forgot** (1975). Director Kevin Connor, who helmed several fantasy adventures in this era, brings Burroughs' lost world vision to life with practical effects and ambitious creature designs despite budget constraints. The film follows the same practical effects tradition as Ray Harryhausen classics like **One Million Years B.C.** (1966) and The Valley of Gwangi (1969), using a combination of puppetry, costumes, and forced perspective to create its prehistoric world.

sections.content: The late 1970s marked the end of an era for practical effects-driven fantasy adventures before the CGI revolution. Films like **The People That Time Forgot** maintained the tradition of physical creature effects pioneered by Willis O'Brien in **The Lost World** (1925) and King Kong (1933). While modern viewers might find the effects dated, they represent important practical filmmaking techniques that influenced later works like **Jurassic Park** (1993), which combined practical and CGI elements.

Patrick Wayne (son of John Wayne) leads the cast as Major Ben McBride, bringing a different energy than Doug McClure's rugged presence in the previous film. The movie's portrayal of primitive societies reflects common 1970s adventure film tropes, similar to those seen in **When Dinosaurs Ruled the Earth** (1970) and **The Land That Time Forgot** (1975), though modern viewers may find some depictions problematic. sections.content: The film's influence can be traced through later lost world adventures, from **Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend** (1985) to elements of **Congo** (1995). While bigger budgets and advanced effects would later dominate the genre, **The People That Time Forgot** represents a crucial bridge between the practical effects era and modern blockbusters. Its DNA can be seen in everything from **Prehistoric Park** (2006) to certain sequences in **King Kong** (2005).
